Nāgavagga 23. Elephants The Elephant Chapter

Attadantavatthu

Ahaṁ nāgova saṅgāme, Like an elephant struck Like an elephant in battle cāpato patitaṁ saraṁ; with arrows in battle, struck by an arrow from a bow, Ativākyaṁ titikkhissaṁ, I shall endure abuse, I will endure criticism dussīlo hi bahujjano. for so many folk are badly behaved. from the immoral multitude.

Dantaṁ nayanti samitiṁ, The well-tamed beast is the one led to the crowd; One who is trained can be led through a crowd, dantaṁ rājābhirūhati; the tamed elephant’s the one the king mounts; one who is trained can be mounted by a king; Danto seṭṭho manussesu, the tamed person who endures abuse a trained person is the best among humans, yotivākyaṁ titikkhati. is the best of human beings. one who endures criticism.

Varamassatarā dantā, Those who have tamed themselves are better Excellent are trained mules, ājānīyā ca sindhavā; than fine tamed mules, well-bred Sindhi horses, Kuñjarā ca mahānāgā, thoroughbreds from Sindh, and enormous elephants; attadanto tato varaṁ. or giant tuskers. but more excellent that those is one who is self-trained.

Hatthācariyapubbakabhikkhuvatthu

Na hi etehi yānehi, For not on those mounts For it is not by means of those vehicles gaccheyya agataṁ disaṁ; would you go to the untrodden place, that one goes in the direction one has never gone; Yathāttanā sudantena, whereas, with the help of one whose self is well tamed, where one who is self-trained, well-trained, danto dantena gacchati. you go there, tamed by the tamed. can go by means of that training.

Parijiṇṇabrāhmaṇaputtavatthu

Dhanapālo nāma kuñjaro, The tusker named Dhanapāla The elephant named Dhanapāla Kaṭukabhedano dunnivārayo; is musky in rut, hard to control. is bitter about being separated, and is hard to restrain; Baddho kabaḷaṁ na bhuñjati, Bound, he eats not a morsel, captive, he does not eat, Sumarati nāgavanassa kuñjaro. for he misses the elephant forest. as he misses the elephant forest.

Pasenadikosalavatthu

Middhī yadā hoti mahagghaso ca, One who gets drowsy from overeating, Lethargic and gluttonous, Niddāyitā samparivattasāyī; fond of sleep, rolling round the bed languid, lazing about, Mahāvarāhova nivāpapuṭṭho, like a great hog stuffed with grain: like an oversized pig that has taken the bait, Punappunaṁ gabbhamupeti mando. that dullard returns to the womb again and again. the fool arrives again and again in the womb.

Sānusāmaṇeravatthu

Idaṁ pure cittamacāri cārikaṁ, In the past my mind wandered In the past this mind would wander, Yenicchakaṁ yatthakāmaṁ yathāsukhaṁ; how it wished, where it liked, as it pleased. going wherever it wished, wherever it desired, wherever it found pleasure. Tadajjahaṁ niggahessāmi yoniso, Now I’ll carefully guide it, Today I will subdue it with a wise understanding of causality, Hatthippabhinnaṁ viya aṅkusaggaho. as a trainer with a hook guides a rutting elephant. like an elephant-trainer subduing a rampaging elephant.

Pāveyyakahatthivatthu

Appamādaratā hotha, Delight in diligence! Approve of non-negligence, sacittamanurakkhatha; Take good care of your mind! and guard your own mind. Duggā uddharathattānaṁ, Pull yourself out of this pit, Lift yourself up from the harmful path, paṅke sannova kuñjaro. like an elephant sunk in a bog. like an elephant lifting itself up from the mud.

Sambahulabhikkhuvatthu

Sace labhetha nipakaṁ sahāyaṁ, If you find an alert companion, If you can get a prudent companion Saddhiṁ caraṁ sādhuvihāridhīraṁ; an attentive friend to live happily together, to travel with, a steadfast person who lives an excellent life, Abhibhuyya sabbāni parissayāni, then, overcoming all adversities, then leave behind all your problems Careyya tenattamano satīmā. wander with them, joyful and mindful. and go with them, satisfied and mindful.

No ce labhetha nipakaṁ sahāyaṁ, If you find no alert companion, If you can not get a prudent companion Saddhiṁ caraṁ sādhuvihāridhīraṁ; no attentive friend to live happily together, to travel with, a steadfast person who lives an excellent life, Rājāva raṭṭhaṁ vijitaṁ pahāya, then, like a king who flees his conquered realm, then like a king leaving behind a conquered realm, Eko care mātaṅgaraññeva nāgo. wander alone like a tusker in the wilds. go alone, like an elephant in its wilderness habitat.

Ekassa caritaṁ seyyo, It’s better to wander alone, It is best to go alone; Natthi bāle sahāyatā; there’s no fellowship with fools. there is no companionship with a fool. Eko care na ca pāpāni kayirā, Wander alone and do no wrong, One who lives alone and does nothing harmful Appossukko mātaṅgaraññeva nāgo. at ease like a tusker in the wilds. will be at ease, like an elephant in its wilderness habitat.

Māravatthu

Atthamhi jātamhi sukhā sahāyā, A friend in need is a blessing; It is pleasant to have companions when the need arises, Tuṭṭhī sukhā yā itarītarena; it’s a blessing to be content with whatever; it is pleasant to be content with whatever comes, Puññaṁ sukhaṁ jīvitasaṅkhayamhi, good deeds are a blessing at the end of life, it is pleasant to have merit when life comes to an end, Sabbassa dukkhassa sukhaṁ pahānaṁ. and giving up all suffering is a blessing. it is pleasant to leave behind all suffering.

Sukhā matteyyatā loke, In this world it’s a blessing to serve It is pleasant to be a mother in this world, atho petteyyatā sukhā; one’s mother and one’s father. it is pleasant to be a father; Sukhā sāmaññatā loke, And it’s a blessing also to serve it is pleasant to be a contemplative in this world, atho brahmaññatā sukhā. ascetics and brahmins. it is pleasant to be spiritual.

Sukhaṁ yāva jarā sīlaṁ, It’s a blessing to keep precepts until you grow old; It is pleasant to have virtue that lasts into old age, sukhā saddhā patiṭṭhitā; a blessing to be grounded in faith; it is pleasant to have established faith, Sukho paññāya paṭilābho, the getting of wisdom’s a blessing; it is pleasant to have attained wisdom, pāpānaṁ akaraṇaṁ sukhaṁ. and it’s a blessing to avoid doing wrong. it is pleasant to do no evil.

Nāgavaggo tevīsatimo.
